source: Daw, Gershman, Seymour, Dayan, Dolan (2011) Model-based influences on humans' choices and striatal prediction errors
finding: The founding two-step result. Choices showed both a reward main effect (model-free) and a reward-by-transition interaction (model-based). Ventral striatal prediction-error signal also carried model-based value.
numbers: N=17. Reward main effect p<1e-8; reward x transition interaction p<5e-5; no transition main effect (p=.5). Per subject: reward effect positive in 14/17, interaction positive in 10/17. Hybrid model beat chance in all 17 (p<.05).
limits: Tiny sample. Weight w is a single constant per person, so it cannot show trial-by-trial arbitration. Later work (b06, b07) shows the 'model-free' part can be an artefact of misunderstanding the task.
agent_relevance: Never assume one clean MB or MF mode. Expect a mix, and measure the mix by behaviour, not by self-report.

source: Momennejad, Russek, Cheong, Botvinick, Daw, Gershman (2017) The successor representation in human reinforcement learning (Exp 1, passive)
finding: Design that separates SR from MB and MF: after relearning, people adapted better to a reward change than to a transition change. MF and MB (or any mix) predict equal adaptation, so only an SR-using learner predicts the gap.
numbers: Exp 1 N=58 (within-subject, 20 games each). Condition effect F(2,1154)=38.77, p<.001. Reward vs transition revaluation t(57)=2.89, Bonferroni p=0.016. Both beat control: t(57)=10.15 and 9.05, p<.001. Control not different from zero t(57)=1.2, p=.22.
limits: The gap is modest (p=.016 after correction). Transition revaluation was still well above control, so people are not pure SR. Passive Pavlovian-style task with preference ratings, not choices.
agent_relevance: Cached 'where does this lead' structure is cheap to reuse when only the payoff changes, and goes stale when the route structure changes. A memory of class-level outcomes needs a staleness check when transitions change.

source: Momennejad et al. (2017), Exp 2 (instrumental) and policy revaluation, as described in review and primary text
finding: The effect replicated in an instrumental multi-step task. A new 'policy revaluation' condition (only rewards change, but the learner's own policy hid the newly valuable state) behaved like transition revaluation, not like reward revaluation.
numbers: Policy revaluation results were similar to transition revaluation and significantly worse than reward revaluation (reported in the Carvalho et al. 2024 review, which I read in full text; the primary paper states people were less sensitive to policy shift than reward shift). Rules out an MB learner with different learning rates for rewards and transitions.
limits: Authors say SR is one of several candidate mechanisms and does not explain all choice behaviour. Exact Exp 2 N not recorded here.
agent_relevance: A cache built under the current policy hides states the policy avoids. When the agent changes strategy, the stored structure may under-represent now-useful branches.

source: Carvalho, Tomov, de Cothi, Barry, Gershman (2024) Predictive representations: building blocks of intelligence (account of Geerts et al. 2024 Kalman TD)
finding: Rival explanation: a Kalman-filter TD learner of the SR with non-local updating can produce the partial transition-revaluation result without model-based simulation. It also explains context pre-exposure facilitation vs latent inhibition.
numbers: Qualitative account. Geerts et al. (2024) is the primary source; I did not open it.
limits: Secondhand. The two accounts (SR plus replay vs Kalman SR) both fit the human data, so the human data do not yet pick one.
agent_relevance: The 'hybrid SR plus offline simulation' design is not forced by the evidence. Updating cached structure from uncertainty may be enough.

source: Momennejad, Otto, Daw, Norman (2018) Offline replay supports planning in human reinforcement learning (abstract read only)
finding: fMRI study of a 2-step revaluation task. Off-task replay evidence predicted later replanning, and sensitivity to uncertainty (unsigned prediction error) predicted replay and replanning.
numbers: Abstract-level only: replay pattern evidence predicts replanning; uncertainty predicts replay. I did not extract N or effect sizes.
limits: Correlational. Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Re-integrate stored structure between episodes, and trigger it by surprise or uncertainty, not on a timer. This matches schema guardrail G1.

source: Feher da Silva & Hare (2020) Humans primarily use model-based inference in the two-stage task (new instructions)
finding: With a detailed story and better instructions, people became mostly model-based. Apparent model-free behaviour in the standard task falls sharply with understanding.
numbers: Spaceship N=21, magic carpet N=24, vs common-instruction data N=206 (Kool). Reward x transition interaction 5.9x larger (95% HDI 4.5-7.3 and 4.7-7.2). Posterior that MB weight is higher >0.9999. Reward effect higher in common instructions: Bayes factor 145 (carpet) and 51 (spaceship).
limits: Small samples per new condition. Model-free influence was reduced, not eliminated. A bigger Bayes factor does not prove the hybrid model is wrong, only that its standard reading is.
agent_relevance: Instruction clarity moves a reasoner from habit-like to model-based behaviour. For an LLM agent, spelling out the transition structure in the prompt is the cheapest lever.

source: Feher da Silva & Hare (2020), simulation and misconception analyses
finding: Purely model-based agents with a wrong task model look like hybrids. Fitting the standard hybrid model then reports false model-free influence. Many humans misunderstood the task.
numbers: Fitted MB weight: correct MB agent median 0.94 (95% 0.74-1.00); unlucky-symbol agent 0.36; transition-dependent-learning-rate agent 0.80. In the N=206 data: w correlated with fit, Spearman rho=0.19, p=0.005; 43% had w<0.1. 111/206 rarely made configuration mistakes, 51/206 made them with probability >0.9 (about 25%).
limits: Simulation shows possibility, not what any one person did. The two misconception models were chosen by the authors.
agent_relevance: A label of 'model-free' from behaviour can mean the model of the world was wrong. For our agent: check whether the stored structure is wrong before blaming a shortcut policy.

source: Akam, Costa, Dayan (2015) Simple plans or sophisticated habits? State, transition and learning interactions in the two-step task
finding: Simulations show model-free strategies can masquerade as model-based in the two-step task when reward location correlates with action value, and small task changes can create false MB signs in the stay-probability analysis.
numbers: Simulation paper, no human N. States that a suggested analysis correction (extra regressors) removes part of the problem.
limits: Does not show humans actually do this. Task design and analysis choices, not nature, produce part of the MB/MF split.
agent_relevance: A benchmark for 'planning' can be passed by a cache. Check any claimed MB gain against a control where the cached shortcut fails.

source: Kool, Cushman, Gershman (2016) When does model-based control pay off?
finding: The standard two-step task gives model-based control almost no payoff, so it cannot test cost-benefit arbitration. A redesigned task did, and people used more MB control in it.
numbers: Five factors found that dilute MB payoff. New task N=199 vs original Daw structure N=207 (MTurk, 125 trials). MB weight vs reward rate: r=0.55 (p<.001) in new task, r=0.10 (p=.15) in original; group difference t(377)=4.71, p<.001.
limits: MTurk, between-subject. Shows adaptation to payoff, not the mechanism of arbitration.
agent_relevance: Pay for planning only when it pays. A controller that routes between cache and simulation should be tested on tasks where simulation actually beats the cache.

source: Gillan, Kosinski, Whelan, Phelps, Daw (2016) Characterizing a psychiatric symptom dimension related to deficits in goal-directed control
finding: Reduced model-based control tracks compulsivity and intrusive thought across the general population. Replicated in a second, larger sample.
numbers: Exp 1 N=548: OCD score beta=-0.040 (SE .02), p=.049, about 14% less MB learning per 1 SD of OCD score; depression beta=-0.016 p=.439; anxiety beta=-0.006 p=.778. Exp 2 N=1413: OCD beta=-0.026 p=.020; eating disorders beta=-0.037 p<.001; impulsivity beta=-0.034 p=.007.
limits: Small effects, p=.049 in the first sample. Uses the MB weight from the standard task, which b06 and b07 say mixes in misunderstanding. Online, self-report.
agent_relevance: Individual differences in MB use are small and noisy. Do not tune an agent to one 'MB weight'.

source: Smittenaar, FitzGerald, Romei, Wright, Dolan (2013) Disruption of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex decreases model-based in favor of model-free control
finding: Theta-burst stimulation of right dlPFC reduced model-based control compared with vertex stimulation, with no clear effect on model-free control.
numbers: N=25, within-subject, three sessions. MB control after right dlPFC vs vertex p=0.01; left dlPFC p=0.89; right vs left difference p=0.13.
limits: Small N. The right-versus-left difference is not significant, so lateralisation is not shown.
agent_relevance: Planning needs a limited, controlled resource (working memory). Taking away that resource pushes behaviour to the cache.

source: Test-retest reliability of reinforcement learning parameters (2024)
finding: Learning parameters from bandit and reversal tasks were poorly reliable across five weeks, while personality and cognitive measures were reliable.
numbers: ICCs .67-.93 for personality and cognition; .02-.52 for bandit task parameters; .01-.71 for reversal task parameters. Mood (stress, happiness) explained some within-person variability.
limits: Not the two-step task, so the MB weight itself is not tested here. Indirect.
agent_relevance: Treat person-level MB/MF scores as unstable. Same warning applies to model-level scores from one run.

source: Neurocognitive basis of model-based decision making and its metacontrol in childhood (2023)
finding: Metacontrol (choosing when to use MB) varied across children and tracked inhibition performance and dlPFC, temporal and parietal cortical thickness. Earlier work cited there found MB signatures rise from age 5 to 11.
numbers: N=69 children aged 6-13; structural MRI subset N=44.
limits: Small, cross-sectional. Correlation with cortical thickness is not causal.
agent_relevance: Knowing when to deliberate is a separate skill from deliberating, and develops later. Our counted detector (G1) plays this role.

source: Dopamine enhances model-free credit assignment through boosting of retrospective model-based inference (2021, eLife)
finding: Levodopa strengthened the use of MB inference to guide MF credit assignment, without changing MF or MB influence directly.
numbers: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject. N not extracted. Drug effect correlated negatively with the change in purely MB credit assignment.
limits: Abstract-level read; N and effect sizes not recorded.
agent_relevance: MB and MF are not walled off. The model can train the cache after the fact, which supports storing lessons from simulated runs.

source: Primate single-neuron study of model-based and model-free RL across prefrontal cortex and striatum (eLife 2026)
finding: In macaques on the two-step task, MB signatures were mainly in ACC, and MF signatures mainly in putamen. DLPFC and caudate also recorded.
numbers: Details from the authors' reply text; unit counts not extracted.
limits: Only the introduction and reviewer reply were read, so figures are unverified.
agent_relevance: Support for separable roles, but the separation is a matter of degree.

source: Russek, Momennejad, Botvinick, Gershman, Daw (2017) Predictive representations can link model-based reinforcement learning to model-free mechanisms
finding: SR and Dyna-style offline replay are two ways a cache-like system can produce model-based behaviour. SR is cheap at decision time but needs a policy and goes stale when transitions change.
numbers: Theory and simulation. Dyna caches V(s) and adds offline updates from model samples or replay of stored episodes.
limits: Simulation, not human data in this paper.
agent_relevance: The two cheap ways to get planning-like behaviour: pre-computed expected-occupancy (SR) or replay between episodes (Dyna). Both fit a memory store.

source: Dayan (1993) Improving generalisation for temporal difference learning: the successor representation
finding: Founding paper. How well values generalise between states is set by how similar their successors are. TD can learn the representation, shown on a navigation task.
numbers: No human data.
limits: Policy-dependent. Cannot adapt to transition changes without new experience.
agent_relevance: Group stored memories by where they lead, not by surface similarity.

source: Carvalho et al. (2024) review: Tomov et al. (2021) multi-task generalisation, as described
finding: Humans on a novel task tended to reuse the training policy that did best on the new reward weights, even when it was not optimal. This 'policy reuse' (generalised policy improvement) is not explained by pure MB or MF.
numbers: Several experiments, one test trial each, task with shared transitions and varied reward weights. Details from the review; I did not open Tomov et al.
limits: Secondhand. One test trial per person.
agent_relevance: Store class-level 'how it turned out' knowledge and reuse the best old plan when the goal changes.

source: Carvalho et al. (2024) review: de Cothi et al. (2022) human and rat navigation, as described
finding: Homologous maze task for rats and humans, 10x10 grid, 25 blocked configurations, 10 trials each. Behaviour of both species was most like an SR agent. Humans also resembled MB. Neither resembled MF.
numbers: Qualitative summary; no coefficients quoted in the review.
limits: Secondhand. Hidden fixed goal; fits depend on the three agent implementations chosen by the authors.
agent_relevance: Spatial detour tasks favour SR-like agents, which suggests cheap predictive maps carry much of everyday planning.

source: Stachenfeld, Botvinick, Gershman (2017) The hippocampus as a predictive map (subgoal section)
finding: SR eigenvectors resemble grid fields and can find bottleneck states that link isolated clusters of states, which are useful subgoals.
numbers: Model simulations; the part I read was the subgoal discovery section.
limits: Simulation of the model; the paper's empirical test is against previously published rodent data, which I did not extract.
agent_relevance: Bottlenecks in the structure graph are good places to set subgoals or checks.

source: Binz & Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3 (two-step task)
finding: GPT-3 showed signs of model-based behaviour on the canonical two-step task, but failed a causal reasoning task and was sensitive to small prompt changes.
numbers: 200 simulated runs, 20 repetitions each. Stay probability fell after a rare-transition reward, t(1982)=-6.16, p<.001; rose after a rare no reward, t(1814)=2.33, p=.01.
limits: A stay-probability test. Per b06, such patterns can also appear when the model is wrong. GPT-3 also gave intuitive-but-wrong answers on the CRT.
agent_relevance: Text-model agents can give MB-like choice patterns in a text game, but robustness is another matter.

source: Coda-Forno, Binz, Wang, Schulz (2024) CogBench: a large language model walks into a psychology lab
finding: Model-basedness on the two-step task rises with model size, and with chain-of-thought and step-back prompting. GPT-4 exceeded human model-basedness.
numbers: Seven tasks, 35 LLMs. Parameters effect beta=0.481 (z=4.2, p<0.001). CoT raised model-basedness by 64.59%, step-back by 118.59%. Code training and data size not significant.
limits: Model-basedness is a regression index on stay probabilities, so b06/b07 caveats apply. Percent gains are relative to base models.
agent_relevance: Step-back prompting (restating the problem structure) gave a larger MB gain than step-by-step reasoning. Supports a restate-first operator.

source: Demircan, Saanum, et al. (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in large language models
finding: Llama-3.1-70B learns two-step task and grid policies in-context with features that track TD error. The same model builds representations closer to the SR than to a transition matrix when watching a random walk.
numbers: Two-step: Q-learning NLL 2729 vs myopic 2864. 8B stays at chance. Random-walk graph (3 communities, 401 observations, 20 repeats): SAE latents correlate with SR max r=0.62 vs transition matrix 0.49; TD error r=0.60 vs surprise r=0.18. Lesioning the TD latent cut next-state accuracy from 24.3% to 18.9%.
limits: Preprint. Correlational, with one causal lesion. Only Llama family. Ability appears with scale.
agent_relevance: Direct support: large models already build SR-like structure from experience in context. An explicit external SR may duplicate it, but the 8B result says small models need help.

source: Momennejad, Hasanbeig, et al. (2023) Evaluating cognitive maps and planning in LLMs with CogEval
finding: Eight LLMs showed apparent planning only on simple graphs where routes could be copied from the prompt. They failed by inventing edges, taking long routes, and looping.
numbers: GPT-4 on 'shortest path 1 cluster away': 0/30 at temperature 0; no more than 10% at temperature 0.5 or 1. BFS or DFS instructions helped on several community-graph tasks. Performance was not stable across graph structure, domain or task.
limits: 2023 models only (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude-1, Bard and others). May not hold for current models.
agent_relevance: Listing edges works; using them to plan across communities does not. Give the agent the code-side graph and search, not the narrative.

source: Fang & Rajan (2025) From memories to maps: mechanisms of in-context RL in transformers
finding: A transformer trained on planning tasks learns strategies that are not readable as standard MF or MB. It caches intermediate computations in memory tokens and reads them at decision time. Its representations resemble hippocampal-entorhinal ones.
numbers: Mechanistic analysis; no human comparison numbers extracted.
limits: Small trained transformer, not a pretrained LLM.
agent_relevance: Cached intermediate results are a third thing, between value cache and full simulation. A stored scratch result by class fits.

source: Baumgartner, Spens, Burgess, Manescu (2025) Cognitive maps in language models: a mechanistic analysis of spatial planning
finding: GPT-2 models trained on random walks form a map-like coordinate code. Models trained only on shortest-path targets learn path-dependent heuristics. A hybrid improved generalisation but kept the path-dependent strategy.
numbers: Three training regimes in grid worlds. No headline accuracy extracted.
limits: Small GPT-2 trained from scratch, not a frontier LLM.
agent_relevance: Exploration-style data builds the map. Goal-only data builds shortcuts. Memory should store transitions seen, not just winning answers.

source: Lampinen et al. (2025) Latent learning: episodic memory complements parametric learning
finding: Parametric learners fail to use information not needed for the current task (the reversal curse is one case). A system with an oracle retrieval mechanism generalises better, and needs within-experience in-context learning to use what it retrieves.
numbers: Several tasks including navigation and reversal. Abstract-level; numbers not extracted.
limits: Oracle retrieval, so real retrieval errors are not included.
agent_relevance: Keep raw episodes and retrieve them, since you cannot know which latent structure will matter.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with language model is planning with world model (RAP)
finding: Using the LLM as a world model and running tree search (model-based) on Blocksworld raised success greatly over chain-of-thought.
numbers: 2/4/6-step Blocksworld: RAP averaged 64% while CoT failed almost completely. LLaMA-33B with RAP beat GPT-4 with CoT by 33% relative improvement.
limits: 2023 models. Search cost much more than a single pass.
agent_relevance: Simulating consequences with a model, then evaluating, beats one-shot reasoning on long-horizon planning.

source: Gu et al. (2024) Is your LLM secretly a world model of the internet? (WebDreamer)
finding: Imagining the outcome of each candidate action with an LLM world model before acting (a cheap MB step) beat reactive baselines. It matched tree search while being cheaper.
numbers: About 45 times more efficient than tree search on VisualWebArena. Dreamer-7B world model comparable to GPT-4o on two online benchmarks.
limits: Web tasks with irreversible actions. Headline numbers beyond efficiency were not extracted.
agent_relevance: One-step lookahead on each candidate is a cheap middle path between acting blind and a full search.

source: Mondal, Webb, et al. (2025) Improving planning with LLMs: a modular agentic architecture (MAP)
finding: Splitting planning into modules (conflict monitor, state predictor, state evaluator, decomposition, orchestrator) improved graph traversal, Tower of Hanoi, PlanBench and strategyQA over zero-shot, ICL, CoT, debate and tree-of-thought.
numbers: Failure analysis on 3-disk Tower of Hanoi: 75% run accuracy, 6/24 unsolved. Failure modes: wrong decomposition, no progress, loops.
limits: Per-benchmark gains not extracted here. Still loops on failure.
agent_relevance: Counted code-level modules beat one long prompt, in line with schema section 1.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Transformers can learn temporal difference methods for in-context RL
finding: A transformer trained on policy evaluation can learn to run TD learning in its forward pass, shown in theory and experiment.
numbers: Abstract-level.
limits: Trained for policy evaluation, not general LLMs.
agent_relevance: Supports the idea that in-context value learning is a real mechanism (see Demircan above).

source: Parks & Alharthi (2026) Predictive maps of multi-agent reasoning: a successor-representation spectrum for LLM communication topologies
finding: An SR of the communication graph (M=(I-P)^-1) was used to predict failure of chain, star and mesh topologies of Qwen2.5-7B agents.
numbers: 12-step state-tracking task, 100 trials. Condition number rs=1.0 vs perturbation robustness; spectral gap rs=0.5 vs consensus; spectral radius rs=-1.0 (inverted) vs cumulative error.
limits: Only three topologies, so a rank correlation of 1.0 means one ordering of three. 7B model. Preprint, one task.
agent_relevance: A cheap structural calculation can predict failure before running anything, but one small test is weak support.

source: Binz et al. (2025) Centaur: a foundation model of human cognition (two-step part)
finding: A language model fine-tuned on human choice data produced simulated two-step trajectories ranging from pure MF to pure MB like people, and captured behaviour on a cover story (magic carpet, Feher da Silva and Hare) absent from training.
numbers: Psych-101 training set; no coefficient quoted for the two-step simulation.
limits: Fits behaviour; does not show that it uses MB or SR computation.
agent_relevance: A model can reproduce the human MB/MF spread by training. Matching human behaviour is not planning ability.
